analysis.title: Monthly Investment Insights: Rotation amid resilient fundamentals (3 November 2026)
key_insights: October tech correction looks like a rotation out of technology rather than a broad equity retreat. The S&P 500 fell 3.4% from its early-October peak, the Nasdaq 100 fell 9.5%, and the equal-weighted S&P 500 gained about 4.5% on the month.
With three-quarters of S&P 500 companies reported, roughly three-quarters beat on revenue and roughly three-fifths beat on earnings. Strong earnings alone did not satisfy investors.

Microsoft was rewarded for cloud growth and improving AI monetization, while Alphabet, Amazon and Meta disappointed. Capex and free cash flow concerns amplified the selling. Zurich reads the correction as scrutiny of investment returns, not weaker technology demand.
US Q3 GDP grew 3.4% QoQ SAAR (Q2: 2.2%), with private investment up 19.4%. Computers and peripheral equipment rose 66.7% and contributed over one-fifth of Q3 GDP growth.
Technology capex is lifting electronics exports across Asian manufacturing economies and Mexico, despite USMCA-related uncertainty.

Higher energy prices and persistent inflation risk should keep central banks restrictive. Credit spreads have widened toward Q2 levels, especially for lower-rated borrowers, and leveraged AI infrastructure providers face financing pressure.
Microsoft's USD 25bn bond issuance was heavily oversubscribed, showing strong demand for financially resilient borrowers.

Zurich prefers equities over credit and cash. It sees credit spreads as relatively unattractive despite the widening, and sees room for equity sentiment to recover on better tech valuations and stabilising government bond yields.

Global growth is robust, and roughly half of global central banks hiked over the past quarter. Government bond yields fell sharply from oversold levels, partly on AI concerns, while oil rose and pushed real yields lower. Zurich says yields are unlikely to fall much further unless oil falls materially.

US headline CPI accelerated to 3.7% YoY on energy. The Fed held in October and signalled another hike in December. Zurich says market pricing of three more hikes looks too aggressive. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 20% in two weeks.

UK Composite PMI rose to 53.1 in October, the highest since February. Headline CPI rose to 3.5% YoY in September from 3.1%, and core CPI rose to 2.8% from 2.6%. Zurich expects tighter policy. Gilt yields eased from multi-year highs after a quiet Autumn Budget.

Eurozone activity is slowing and unemployment is rising. Natural gas is above 100 EUR/MWh and Zurich expects 2027 inflation above 3%. It sees a December ECB hike as likely. French yields have surged, France's economy shrank in Q3, and Zurich sees risks skewed negatively for French and Italian assets.
Switzerland: growth is strong on the global capex cycle and headline CPI is 1%. The franc has strengthened on Eurozone political risk. Zurich expects modest SNB tightening over the coming year.

Japan: the BoJ is increasingly confident inflation is sustainably near target and Zurich expects a December hike. The Nikkei underperformed TOPIX on the tech rotation. Zurich stays constructive on Japanese stocks, and long-end JGB yields eased on institutional demand.

China: equities fell sharply in October and 'National Team' buying followed. Zurich thinks the market may be nearing a trough, stays neutral, and sees the RMB 25tn five-year 'six network' infrastructure programme as too small to reflate the economy.

Australia: data centre investment supports growth, but four rate hikes this year, energy prices and a housing correction pose downside risks. The cancelled Firmus IPO signals investor selectivity on AI valuations. Zurich expects Australian stocks to stay rangebound.

EM Asia: SK Hynix beat Q3 estimates and Samsung missed slightly, and Samsung was punished for the miss and delayed capital returns. MSCI's consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone Market status triggered a steep equity slide, with a decision due June 2027. Zurich stays positive on tech.

LatAm equities fell 7.7% in October. Brazil fell 12.1% after Lula's surprise runoff victory weakened fiscal consolidation expectations, Mexico rose 4.4% and Chile fell 9.9%. Zurich is neutral on Brazilian equities.
